extracted.intended_audience: Developers/contributors writing Python/Cython code and documentation for Sage (SageMath)
extracted.subtask_description: Conventions and requirements for writing, documenting, and testing Python/Cython code that is included in the Sage library, including file headers, docstring structure, formatting, and automated doctest practices. Intended for developers contributing code and documentation to the Sage project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow standard Python formatting rules (PEP8/PEP257)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the standard Python formatting rules when writing code for Sage, as explained in PEP-8 and PEP-257.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 4 spaces for indentation levels (no tabs). Many editors can replace tabs with 4 spaces. Use all-lowercase function names with words separated by underscores (e.g. def set_some_value()). Use CamelCase for class names and major functions that create objects (e.g. PolynomialRing). Some existing functions may have uppercase letters where appropriate (example: Matrix_integer_dense.LLL).

rubrics_metrics.name: File and directory naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Python Sage library code uses specific naming conventions for files and directories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directory names may be plural (e.g. rings) and file names are almost always singular (e.g. polynomial_ring.py). A file may still contain definitions of several different related types. Follow existing examples in the Sage library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-of-file heading and header template
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Sage code file should begin with a standardized header consisting of an r""" docstring summary, description, AUTHORS list, EXAMPLES, then copyright and license boilerplate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The header should include: a very short one-line summary, a paragraph description, an AUTHORS section with entries using ISO date format and brief notes on changes, EXAMPLES, and then the copyright and GPL-style license block. Follow the example template shown in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: License requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All code included with Sage must be licensed under the GPLv2+ or a less restrictive license (e.g., the BSD license).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include proper copyright/license boilerplate at top of files. Also include your name in the AUTHORS log so contributors receive credit; notify the development team if you feel credit is missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every function must have a docstring
rubrics_metrics.description: Every function must have a docstring that includes specified sections and formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Docstrings should contain: a one-sentence description (followed by a blank line), INPUT and OUTPUT blocks, an EXAMPLES block (mandatory), optional ALGORITHM, NOTES, WARNING, REFERENCES, and AUTHORS blocks as appropriate. Use many examples since these are used for automatic testing; new functions without doctests will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: INPUT and OUTPUT block format
rubrics_metrics.description: Docstrings must include INPUT and OUTPUT blocks describing inputs, outputs, and defaults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type names should be descriptive (e.g., 'integer' rather than precise Python types). For each parameter use a bullet line like ``- ``p`` -- (default: 2) a positive prime integer.`` OUTPUT block can be a descriptive paragraph or a dashed bullet list. Alternatively, use Sphinx/ReST info-field lists (e.g., :param:, :type:, :returns:, :rtype:) as described in Sphinx documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: EXAMPLES block is mandatory and doctested
rubrics_metrics.description: Each docstring must include an EXAMPLES block; these examples are used for automatic testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include code examples that demonstrate typical usage and exceptions. There must be a blank line after the example code and before explanatory text. Examples are automatically tested before each release; without doctests new functions will not be accepted. Use examples liberally and ensure they run under the standard Sage prompt.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALGORITHM block (optional) and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an ALGORITHM block when describing algorithms, with optional numbering of steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ALGORITHM is optional but should state what software/algorithm is used and cite references. You can number steps using the hash-dot symbol (#.) so numbering is handled automatically. Provide references and adapt examples shown in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: NOTES block formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional NOTES block should start with a ReST info field and be indented properly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with ``.. NOTE::`` (lower-case ``.. note::`` is allowed but don't mix cases). Indent content at least 4 spaces (no tabs). Use NOTES for purpose or caveats; follow indentation rules exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: WARNING block formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional WARNING block should be used for critical information about the code and its limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with ``.. WARNING::`` (lower-case allowed but upper-case preferred). Use this block to indicate when or under which conditions the code might break or other critical caveats. Indent content appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: REFERENCES block usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional REFERENCES block to list books or papers used by the method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ReST/Sphinx citation markup for references (see Sphinx docs). List standard references for algorithms or methods under REFERENCES.

rubrics_metrics.name: AUTHORS block in docstring
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an AUTHORS block in the docstring (optional but encouraged) to document authorship and contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the template with entries like ``- William Stein (2005-01-03)``. AUTHORS help users know whom to contact about the function; include your name so you receive credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docstring Sphinx/ReST alternative markup
rubrics_metrics.description: Docstrings may use Sphinx/ReST :param:, :type:, :returns:, :rtype: markup instead of INPUT/OUTPUT blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using Sphinx/ReST, follow the described formats (examples shown). Use :param name: description and :type name: type; :returns: and :rtype: for return values.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX/Math formatting guidance in docstrings
rubrics_metrics.description: You are strongly encouraged to use nice LaTeX formatting but balance LaTeX with interactive readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using backslashes in docstrings either double them (\\) or use a raw string (r"""...) to avoid escaping. You can also use the .. MATH:: block for complicated expressions. However, since docstrings are viewed interactively with backslashes stripped, prefer readable forms (e.g., use 'a/b' or 'a b^{-1}' rather than '\\frac{a}{b}'). Use provided local macros like \ZZ, \RR, \GF, \Zmod and see $SAGE_ROOT/devel/sage/sage/misc/latex_macros.py for the full list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive-help vs. reference-manual tradeoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Docstrings serve both interactive help and typeset reference manual purposes; strike a balance between LaTeX and readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly complicated LaTeX in docstrings because some users don't know LaTeX and interactive display strips backslashes. Use simple expressions when possible to be user-friendly in interactive help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples must illustrate exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Show exception behavior in examples to document error conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include doctest examples that demonstrate exceptions (use the 'Traceback' form). For instance, show that passing an invalid type raises TypeError with the example pattern used in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid putting crucial docs in underscore-named functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions whose names start with an underscore do not currently appear in the reference manual, so avoid putting crucial documentation only in their docstrings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If defining a class, consider placing a long informative docstring after the class definition rather than in __init__, because methods or functions starting with underscores may be omitted from the reference manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated testing requirement for examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Code in examples should pass automatic testing via the sage -t framework; examples are executed with Sage preparsing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sage -t <file> to test examples. The testing script (SAGE_LOCAL/bin/sage-doctest) creates .doctest files with Sage preparsing applied and runs them. Tests are run as if examples were entered at the sage: prompt with from sage.all import * at the top. Ensure examples are runnable without requiring special imports unless included in the example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing files of various types (.py, .pyx, .sage, .rst)
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated testing supports .py, .pyx, .sage, and .rst files; ReST verbatim environments are also tested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run sage -t <filename.rst> to test examples in ReST verbatim blocks. To link verbatim blocks use ``.. link::``. Use ``.. skip::`` to skip a verbatim environment. See tutorial files for examples of including automated testing in ReST docs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use SAGE_TMP and os.path.join for file outputs in tests
rubrics_metrics.description: If a test writes to files, the file should be in a temporary directory accessible during testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SAGE_TMP (always defined during automated testing) and os.path.join(SAGE_TMP, 'filename') to construct output file paths. If using SAGE_TMP in code (not only in doctests), import it appropriately. Avoid hard-coded or Unix-specific paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctest tags and their behavior (#random, # long time, #optional, todo)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special tags in doctest examples control whether outputs are checked or whether tests are run under normal testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a test line contains 'random', sage-doctest executes it but does not check output against the docstring. Lines with 'long time' are not tested unless sage -t -long is used; include these for examples that take long. Lines with 'todo: not implemented' are never tested — use to indicate desired but missing features. Lines or blocks with 'optional' are not tested unless -optional flag is passed (useful for examples requiring optional packages). If an entire docstring contains 'optional', 'package', and 'installed' the whole docstring is skipped unless -optional is passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomized testing best practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider creating a randomized test suite to exercise code with random inputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a test class Test with a random() method that runs randomized tests for some time. These tests are assembled and run regularly to try to crash code using randomly generated inputs. See example test files in the Sage repository and the development map for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sage preparsing behavior for examples
rubrics_metrics.description: All input in doctest examples is preparsed before being passed to Python.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, '2/3' in an example is replaced by Integer(2)/Integer(3) so that it evaluates as rational 2/3 rather than Python integer division. Understand preparsing effects when writing examples and tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing sanity: files are not imported when testing unless available in environment
rubrics_metrics.description: When running sage -t <file>, the file is not imported unless its functions are available when starting Sage using the sage command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure examples either import the module or are written so they run when entered at the sage prompt. If your function is not known by default, include an import line in the example so the doctest can find it (see cdd_convert example).
